 Judgment

This petition is filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- from the respondents on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :

On 30-12-2018 at about 9.15 a.m., the petitioner was a pedestrian from Karnataka Bank towards No.156 Sharada Mansion Complex, on the extreme left side, on R. V.
Road.

While he was crossing the said road near Minarva Junction, carefully observing the vehicle movements, suddenly the rider of scooter bearing No.
KA-05-JZ-7284 came from Lalbagh West Gate towards Minarva Circle, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery.

Earlier to the accident, he was working as weaver at Kumar Silk,
Bengaluru and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he became permanently disabled and whereby lost his earning capacity.
The V.V. Puram Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said two- wheeler for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsels and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has denied the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the motorcycle bearing No.
KA-05-JZ-7284 in the alleged accident.

He has further denied the age, income and avocation of the Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
2 petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.

Further he has contended that,
his son by name Ajay rode the motorcycle bearing No. KA-05- JZ-7284, the accident has not occurred on the extreme left side of the R.V. Road and on the date of accident, the petitioner without taking proper care and caution all of sudden was crossing the road, at the place where it was prohibited for crossing of road.
He was crossing the road from East to West direction, towards opposite to BMTC bus- stop, situated on the Lalbagh towards Minarva Circle road.
While crossing the road the petitioner had noticed that the BMTC bus, which was standing on the bus stop, has started and all of sudden he came back in reverse direction and touched the motorcycle.
The rider of the motorcycle applied the break suddenly and in this process he also fell down and sustained the injuries.
The petitioner himself is responsible for the accident and rider of the motorcycle never rode his scooter in negligent manner and he was not responsible for the accident.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. Likewise, the respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has contended that, the respondent No.1 willfully entrusted his vehicle bearing No.
KA-05-JZ-7284 to the person who did not had valid and effective driving licence to ride the said vehicle, as on the date of accident.

The jurisdictional police after due investigation have filed the charge-sheet against the rider and owner of the said scooter under Section 3(1) R/w Sec.181 and Sect.5 R/w Sec.180 of Motor Vehicles Act, wherein it is mentioned that, as on the date of accident the accused No.1/rider of the scooter did not had a valid and effective driving licence to ride the same and accused No.2/ owner of the scooter allowed/entrusted the same to a person who was not holding licence to ride the scooter.
Hence, there is breach and violations of the terms and conditions of the policy.

It has further contended that, the accident in question took place solely due to the carelessness and negligence of the petitioner, who was darting across the road without observing the flow of traffic on the busy road.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of scooter bearing No.KA-05-JZ-7284 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident alleged to have occurred on 30-12-2018 at about 9.15 a.m., due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing registration No. KA- 05-JZ-7284 ?

7. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.
Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. Somashekar as P.W.2 and closed his side.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has got examined himself as R.W.1 and his son/driver of offending vehicle as R.W.2 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3.

Likewise, the Respondent No.2 insurance company has got examined its official as R.W.3 and got marked 7 documents as Ex.R.4 to 10.
8.

I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Partly Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, 30-12-2018 at about 9.15 a.m., the petitioner was a pedestrian from Karnataka Bank towards No.156 Sharada Mansion Complex, on the extreme left side, on R. V. Road.

While he was crossing the said road near Minarva Junction, carefully observing the vehicle movements, suddenly the rider of scooter bearing No. KA-05-JZ-7284 came from Lalbagh West Gate towards Minarva Circle, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, due to the accidental injuries he had become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
11. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of F.I.R and first information statement,
Ex.P.2 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.3 are certified copies of plea (total 2), Ex.P.4 are certified copies of charge-sheet (total 2), Ex.P.5 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of sketch, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of Notice U/Sec.133 M.V.Act, Ex.P.8 is certified copy of M.V.A report, Ex.P.9 is certified copy of reply to notice U/Sec.133 M.V.Act, Ex.P.10 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.11 are medical bills (total 20), Ex.P.12 are discharge summaries issued by KIMS Hospital (total 2), Ex.P.13 is salary certificate, Ex.P.14 are X-rays (total 4), Ex.P.15 is out patient registration, Ex.P.16 and 17 are in-patient records (total 2) and Ex.P.18 are X-rays.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 10, prima-facia it reveals that, on 30-12- 2018 at about 9.15 a.m., the petitioner was a pedestrian from Karnataka Bank towards No.156 Sharada Mansion Complex, on R. V. Road.

While he was crossing the said road near Minarva Junction, the rider of offending scooter bearing No. KA-05-JZ-7284 came from Lalbagh West Gate towards Minarva Circle, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

13. The investigation officer has filed the charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-JZ-7284, for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of I.P.C., and Sec.180, 181,
187 R/w Sec.3(1) & 5 of Motor Vehicles Act.

As per the said charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.2,
the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-05-JZ-7284 and at the time of accident the rider of said vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

But, on the other hand, the petitioner/injured in the said accident has himself unequivocally admitted in his cross-examination that, the said accident has occurred due to his own negligence and if he had taken care and try to cross the road cautiously by observing the vehicle movement, the said accident would not have occurred.

Further,
he has clearly admitted that, at the place of accident there were no pedestrian crossing mark or zebra mark to cross the road and even there were no traffic signals at the said place.
Further he has admitted that, the place of accident is a heavy traffic road and he did not see the offending motorcycle proceeding towards him.

14. The investigation officer has clearly stated in his final report that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA-05-JZ-7284.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8, the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicle involved in the accident.
When the accident was not due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to negligence of the rider of offending vehicle.

The final report submitted by the investigation officer and other police documents available on record and the above noted admissions in the cross-examination of petitioner, clearly establishes that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA- 05-JZ-7284 and the pedestrian/petitioner in the cause of accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.10 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summaries, Ex.P.14 X- ray films, Ex.P.15 out-patient registration, Ex.P.16 and 17 in- patient records and Ex.P.18 X-rays, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered Type-II compound fracture left leg both the bone, wound over antero lateral aspect of left leg.
There is absolutely no material or rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents which creates doubt on the medical records or to disbelieve the evidence led by the petitioner.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
5 criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied."

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 30-12-2018 at about 9.15 a.m., at Minarva Junction, near Lalbagh West Gate, Bengaluru, but, failed to prove that the said accident has occurred due to the sole rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing registration No. KA-05-JZ-7284.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Partly Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident occurred on 30-12-2018 at about 9.15 a.m., at Minarva Junction, near Lalbagh West Gate, Bengaluru, caused by the offending scooter bearing registration No. KA-05-JZ-7284.

Further, it is held that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA-05-JZ-7284 and the pedestrian/ petitioner in the cause of accident.

Further, the petitioner has proved that, he has sustained Type-II compound fracture left leg both the bone, wound over antero lateral aspect of left leg and for the said injuries he has underwent surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for 50% of total compensation awarded under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.,

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has not produced any relevant document.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, at one instant the petitioner has mentioned his age in the petition as 53 years and at the other instant in the examination-in-chief affidavit, he has mentioned his age as 62 years.
Whereas, in the cross-examination, the petitioner himself admits that, his age is wrongly mentioned in the examination-in-chief affidavit and his actual age is 67 years.

If the age of the petitioner is taken as 67 years as on the date of recording his cross-examination i.e.
on 26-05-2022, then the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident i.e.
30-12-2018, was 63 years.

As there is no document produced by the petitioner to prove his actual age as on the date of accident, the age admitted by the petitioner in his cross-examination, which is at higher side, is taken into consideration and his age as on the date of accident is considered as 63 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined and treated the petitioner has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered Type-II compound fracture left leg both the bone, wound over antero lateral aspect of left leg measuring 3x2 cms., and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. wound debridement, primary closure, closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has 35% physical disability of left lower limb and for the whole body he has 11.67% physical disability.
The oral evidence of P.W.2 is fully corroborated with documentary evidence.
The Ex.P.10 wound certificate, Ex.P.12 discharge summaries, Ex.P.14 X- ray films, Ex.P.15 out patient registration, Ex.P16 and 17 inpatient records (total 2) and Ex.P.18 x-rays

, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and he has suffered Type-II compound fracture left leg both the bone, wound over antero lateral aspect of left leg measuring 3x2 cms., and for the said injuries the petitioner has underwent surgery i.e. wound debridement, primary closure, closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing for left tibia.
Though, the learned counsel for respondents No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.

Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the Ex.P.15 to 18 documents are not related to the petitioner, there is no disability suffered by him and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability to the petitioner.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 30-12-2018 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 15-07- 2023, which is after lapse of four and half year from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.
Further he has stated that, the the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of the implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the fractures of the petitioner are united with implants in situ.
Therefore, considering the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence on record, this Court is of the opinion that,
considering the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified
. Hence, in the instant case the disability of 10% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
b) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as Weaver at Kumar Silk, Bengaluru and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Further, he has deposed that,
due to grievous injuries suffered in the accident he is unable to do weaver work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
In this regard the petitioner has produced salary certificate issued by Chetaan Silk Sarees, as per Ex.P.13.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
The petitioner has not examined the author of the said document to prove its contents and to prove that it is issued by the authorised person.
Further, there is nothing on record to show that, before accident the petitioner was working as weaver.
In such circumstances, notional income is to be considered as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2018.

Hence, the notional income of the Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
7 petitioner is considered as Rs.12,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,50,000/-.

c) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 63 years is 7.

Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,50,000 X 10/100 X 7 = Rs.1,05,000/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.1,50,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 20 medical bills, as per Ex.P.11.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that, the bills at serial No.4, 5, 10, 12 and 13 are deposit receipts.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.

Accordingly, it is held that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs. 66,437/- towards medical expenses and he is entitled for the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his left leg i.e. Type-II compound fracture left leg both the bone, wound over antero lateral aspect of left leg measuring 3x2 cms.

As per Ex.P.12 discharge summaries, Ex.P.16 and 17 in-patient records, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 19 days from 30-12-2018 to 11-01-2019 and 06-02-2019 to 11-02-2019, in KIMS Hospital and Research Centre, Bengaluru.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.40,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

21. Now the question before this Court is, who is liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of offending scooter bearing Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
9 Reg. No. KA-05-JZ-7284 the accident has occurred.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damages caused by the said vehicle.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
22.

The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently argued that, the Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy clearly speaks that, the policy covers the risk provided the driver of offending vehicle holds an effective driving licence at the time of accident and is not disqualified from holding or obtaining such a licence.

Further, the Ex.P.2 charge-sheet clearly speaks that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, the accused/rider of the offending scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-05-JZ-7284, rode the said vehicle without having valid driving licence and hence in addition to the offence under Sec.279, 338 I.P.C., he has been charge-sheeted for offence U/Sec.181 R/w Sec.3(1) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further, the owner and rider of offending scooter bearing Reg. No. KA- 05-JZ-7284,
who have been examined as R.W.1 and R.W.2, have unequivocally admitted in their cross-examination that, as on the date of alleged accident the R.W.2 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
It is pertinent to note that, R.W.2 is none other than the son of R.W.1.

In such circumstances, the respondent No.1/owner of offending vehicle, who consciously handed over his vehicle to a person who did not possess driving licence, cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

In support of his arguments learned counsel for respondent No.2 relied on the following decisions:
i) Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Lts., and another, in M.F.A. No.6154/2019 (MV-D), judgment dated 14-12-2023, Para No.29, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has held that,
" The owner of the vehicle neither contested the petition by filing written statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that, he did not consciously permit Arun Kumar to ride the vehicle.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act,

Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager V/s Yallavva and another, reported in ILR 2020 Kar 2239, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has clearly held that, " i) Having regard to Section 149(1) R/w Section 149(7), whenever a case falls under Section 149(2)(a) and the same is successfully established or proved by the Insurance Company, as per the twin tests laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Swaran Singh, nevertheless, the insurer or Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the award vis--vis a third party and is entitled to recover from the insured.

sentences.text:
This is irrespective of, the policy being an Act policy in terms of Section 147 pertaining to compulsory coverage of risks of third parties and other classes of persons stated therein or a policy covering other risks by specific contract being entered into in that regard and where additional premium is paid by the insured i.e., a contractual policy.
ii) The Insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under Section 149 (2), even if it is a fundamental breach (that is breach of condition which is the cause for the accident)
and the insurer proves the said breach in view of the mandate under Section 149(1) of the Act.

But, no such order can be passed against the insurer, if, on the facts and circumstances of a case, a finding is given by the court that the third party (injured or deceased) had played any fraud or was in collusion with the insured, individually or collectively, for a wrongful gain to themselves or cause wrongful loss to the insurer.

iii) The Court can also fasten the absolute liability on the insurer, if there is any breach of condition which is enumerated under Section 149(2) of the Act or any other condition of the policy if the Insurance Company has waived breach of any such condition or has taken the special responsibility to pay by collecting extra premium by covering any type of risk depending upon facts of each case.
iv) Thus, the rule of pay and recover is applicable in view of the mandate in Section 149(4) of the Act and even if there is a breach of the terms of the insurance policy, the insurer is bound to satisfy the judgment and award as if it were a judgment debtor,
even if it satisfies the twin tests enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court under Section 149(4)(a) of the Act.
Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
11 v) Before passing any order on the Insurance Company to pay and recover, the Court has to examine the facts and circumstances of each case and if it finds that the victim,
injured or the deceased, in a particular case, was solely or jointly responsible for breach of such fundamental condition by playing fraud or in collusion with the insured, the Court may exercise its discretion not to fasten the liability on the insurer.
vi) However, the court should not adopt the above guideline as a general rule in all cases, but only under peculiar facts and circumstances of each case and on giving appropriate reasons.
vii) If the Insurance Company makes out a case under Section 149(2)(b) of the Act,
then also the Insurance Company has to satisfy the award so far as third party is concerned, as it is the duty of the Insurance Company to indemnify the insured on the basis of the policy of the insurance and even when the contract of insurance itself is void, nevertheless the liability to indemnify the insured would arise and insurer is entitled to recover from the insured.
viii) Thus, in a case where Section 149(2)(b) applies and the Insurance Company successfully establishes that the policy is void, in such a case also, the insurer is not absolved of its liability to satisfy the judgment or award as rights or obligations would flow even from a policy which is void vis--vis third party.

In such a case, the insurer is not completely absolved of its liability, the insured would have to satisfy the award vis--vis the third party and recover from the insured the amount paid to the third party and may also have a right to seek damages from the insured.

ix) The judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in Subramanyam, holding that a pay and recovery order cannot be made as there is no liability to pay or satisfy the award or decree in respect of a case falling under Section 149(2) is not correct.

Hence,
that portion of the judgment in Subramanyam, which states that if the case falls within the scope of Section 149(2) of the Act and the insurer is successful in establishing any of the defences as stated therein, it would be completely absolved of its liability to satisfy the award is also not correct and to that extent, it is held to be bad in law.

24. Admittedly, in the instant case, as on the date of alleged accident the rider of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-05-JZ-7284, was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.

But, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 does not holds good and the observations and ratio laid down in the above cited decisions relied by him are not applicable to case in hand.

On the other hand, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioner holds good and the observations and ratio laid down in the above cited decisions relied by him are aptly applicable to case in hand.

Therefore,
for the above stated reasons and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, this Court comes to conclusion that, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner and later recover the same Narayanaswamy.A vs Narendra Babu.K.L on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145236886/
12 from the owner of offending vehicle/respondent No.1. Accordingly, holding that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,57,319/- from the respondent No.2, with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.

ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.1,57,319/- (Rupees one lakh fifty seven thousand three hundred and nineteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.1 in the very proceedings by filing an execution petition.
The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be released in favour of the petitioner through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
